title: What Happens When You Hit Snooze?
description:
Send this to the friend who sets five alarms.
That groggy fog after your alarm is called sleep inertia, and it usually lasts 15 to 60 minutes (Cleveland Clinic). In an app study of about 3 million nights, about 56% ended in a snooze, and the light sleep between alarms breaks up the REM-rich sleep near morning (Mass General Brigham, Scientific Reports 2025). Twist: in a Stockholm lab study, regular snoozers given a 30-minute snooze did a bit better on cognitive tests right after waking, with no clear effect on mood or sleepiness (Journal of Sleep Research 2023; habitual snoozers only). Experts still suggest setting your alarm for the latest time you can and getting up on the first one.
